recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-8490 unless a future work group decision wants additional stylistic rewording of general Timing narrative text.
issue_request: FHIR-8490 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 FHIR-core datatypes. It requested correcting contradictory Timing wording that said both "Event occurs frequency times per duration" and "Event occurs frequency times per period", and improving the before-meals example so duration and period did not both appear as 10 minutes.
initial_application: The same frequency wording was corrected by related Published issue FHIR-8102 in svn revision 6035, and FHIR-8490 itself was applied in svn revision 6611 by commit ff4f5844ef2a0b69f40884f3b6e04db8e3b69745, which changed the example text from "For 10 minutes before meals" to "For 5 minutes, 10 minutes before meals".
additional_context: Timing is an active datatype in source/fhir.ini and is published on datatypes.html. Later Published issue FHIR-8697 introduced Timing.repeat.offset handling and updated the before-meals example to use offset rather than period. Community searches found no Zulip or Confluence evidence changing this conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/datatypes/timing.xml uses "per period" in the Timing frequency and period definitions, and source/datatypes.html shows the before-meals example with duration 5 min, when AC, offset 10, and no period value.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published Timing issue corrected the same "per duration" wording to "per period".
Later Published Timing issue introduced offset handling and removed the old use of period as the before-meals offset.
